key_insight: A founder population GWAS in Arab ICU patients identified a rare loss-of-function start-loss variant in UBE2L3 that was enriched in sepsis cases and may implicate UBE2L3 in infection susceptibility.
clinical_relevance: The finding suggests a potential genetic risk marker and drug-target hypothesis for sepsis, but it is not ready for clinical use without replication and functional validation.
method: WGS-based GWAS and exome-wide association analysis in 210 Arab ICU patients
Prioritized rare deleterious founder variants using Firth regression, CADD, SIFT, and allele-frequency enrichment
Cross-checked UBE2L3 signal against All of Us bacterial infection burden and AI target-scoring tools
evidence_signal: The strongest case-level signal was a UBE2L3 start-loss variant seen in 3/68 sepsis cases versus 0/142 controls (Fisher’s exact P=0.026), with supportive external burden evidence in All of Us (SKAT-O P=2.38×10^-3).
watch_item: Small sample size and very wide confidence intervals mean the UBE2L3 association needs independent replication before any translational or therapeutic use.
paper_title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Sepsis Susceptibility in ICU Patients Identifies Arab Founder Loss-of-Function Variant in UBE2L3
